observations: The page number «87» stands at the head of the page, centred, with a rule below it. The page has no signature. L01-L05 continue the sentence that ends p. 86 (JP2 0118, L30), «Wir finden nun in Tafel 76 zu diesem Argument der Breite (mit Hilfe der Interpolation) folgende Daten :», with the values of Table 76 (L02) and, after «in Tafel 74 folgende :» (L03), those of Table 74 (L04).

L01-L05: set in three columns: the heads of L01 in the smaller type, ending with a full stop after «Mora»; the values centred under them; rules under the values of L04, and the differences (L05) below them, «Differenzen :» at the left margin. «20dig. 14′»: the abbreviation «dig.» raised, in the smaller type. Each printed row is one line here, the cells separated by our «|»; the empty first cells give «Differenzen :» its column and are not printed. Checked: 20 dig. 14′ − 19 dig. 16′ = 0 dig. 58′; 34′ 45″ − 29′ 39″ = 5′ 6″; 27′ 8″ − 21′ 2″ = 6′ 6″. The values of Tables 74 and 76 are to be compared with the tables.

Between L14 and L15 two figures side by side; they are not reproduced; L15 has their captions, «Fig. 1.» and «Fig. 2.», each centred under its figure. Fig. 1: a large semicircle, the earth's shadow, on a base line with E at its left end, S at its middle and K at its right end; a vertical line from S upwards through A, M and C; a small circle, the moon, about M, which lies on the large semicircle, A the lowest and C the highest point of the small circle. Fig. 2: the same semicircle with E, S and K; the vertical line from S upwards through A, M, B and C, B where it meets the semicircle and C above it; the small circle about M lies within the semicircle, A its lowest point; M is marked with a short stroke across the line. The letters are italic.

L12-L21. Checked: with R the radius of the shadow, r that of the moon and SM the distance of their centres, the latitude of the moon, SC = R + r, and SC − SM = R + r − SM is the depth of the moon's limb within the shadow: in Fig. 2, CM = SC − SM, and AB = SB − SA = R − (SM − r) = CM; in Fig. 1, where M lies on the edge of the shadow, CM = r = AM. Twelve digits make the diameter of the moon, so that the magnitude in digits is (R + r − SM) × 12 : 2r, the depth in minutes times twelve divided by the diameter in minutes, as L19-L21 say.

L22-L29: the Latin terms of chapter 33 of the text (p. 26, JP2 0058, L15-L17): «casus» for «elzukut» (al-suqūṭ), «respiratio» for «elingile» (al-injilāʾ), «mora» for «elmukdh» (al-mukth); here «suḳūṭ», with dots under ḳ and ṭ, «mukth», «makth», «indjilā’», with the macron and the apostrophe of the hamza, in italics. The Greek «ἔμπτωσις» (with the smooth breathing and the acute on the ε) and «μονή», in italics.
L07: the A of «Aus» is an italic sort in the roman line, sloping and of the italic form; transcribed «Aus». L26: «(Mora)» upright.

The dashes: L28 «Verfinsterung. — Im», the long dash with a space on either side; N01 «25—98», the long dash of the small type of the notes (29 px, with gaps of 7 and 9 px). Spaced type, marked {sp:}: «Batt.», «Kh.», «Nallino»; italics also «Digiti» (L08, L21; upright in L14), «partialer», «totaler», the letters of the figures in L12-L19, «Casus», «Mora», «respiratio».
The colons, semicolons and the question mark stand after the thin space of the edition (9-14 px measured; «Daten ?» 13 px).
